checks: The original source-reviewed theorem inventory passes a separate validator invocation and its bytes match the inventory-review hash. The final census preserves all three complete theorem records and their source order.
The pinned PDF hash, version stamp, cover date, authors and 36-page count were checked. Appendix A begins on page 18; all extracted statement evidence is above the documented main-text endpoint.

Theorem 1 includes both bounds, the positive-constant declaration, the penalty condition and the additional depth infimum in (11). Theorem 4 includes its full continuation and penalty rate. Theorem 5 retains its printed grammar and N-based complexity term.

Thirteen source interface passages were reviewed against the pinned main-text pages, including the conditional mean, split objective, candidate success probability, recursive tree and node output, finite ridge variation/library, relaxed local norm, pruning, Assumptions 2-4 and the forest.

Twelve auxiliary passages preserve empirical versus population norms, expectation scope, the uniform q convention, sample-size dependent A/V, finite-dictionary notices and the formal empty-node convention.

The separate census validator accepts all local and canonical edges, source keywords, original highlights and every same-paper theorem explanation. Independently specified scope checks confirm 21 direct uses and 32 deduplicated related-theorem connections.

Pruning reaches only Theorems 1 and 4, Assumptions 3/4 reach only Theorem 4, and forest construction reaches only Theorem 5. The general oracle bounds do not acquire Assumption 1, a mu-in-F condition, or consistency corollary regimes.
The finite ridge-expansion sum precedes G and its L2 closure/relaxed norm in the local graph. The source ambiguity between those norm notations is recorded without rewriting the original definitions.

The forest uses without-replacement subsamples of size N and independent randomization copies sharing the original data. Its RHS success probabilities are interpreted using the subsampled-data convention explicitly stated after Theorem 5.

Source ambiguities are kept in a separate analysis artifact, including the finite norm notation, partition indexing, projection endpoints, pruning wording, depth-uniform node-count condition and degenerate split/probability conventions. Mathematical fragments have balanced braces.

unresolved_source_references.detail: Section 2.1 prints h(x)=sum h_k(x), then sums V(h_k,a_k,t), with directions a_k not bound in that displayed expansion and the node t suppressed in the norm notation. The following relaxed norm uses ridge expansions explicitly. The source passages are kept intact. The dependency graph uses the finite-sum construction for the finite library before the closure/relaxed-norm construction; this is an interpretation of the source staging, not a claim that the notation is fully unambiguous.

The source calls these functionals norms. Constant functions have zero variation, so they are seminorms unless an additional quotient or normalization is intended. No such change is made to the source definitions. F is an L2 closure, and finite relaxed variation for every member is not explicitly asserted.
The text defines |A| as cardinality, but writes a partition P={z_0,...,z_|P|}, containing |P|+1 points. The sum and indexing are preserved rather than silently renumbered.

The projection interval uses min/max even though tree cells can be relatively open or unbounded. Infinite endpoints are explicitly allowed, but endpoint evaluation of h and finite unattained extrema are not given conventions. No replacement by infimum/supremum or truncation is inserted into the quotation.

The printed smallest-minimizer explanation says T_opt precedes every pruned subtree, without limiting the comparison to minimizing subtrees. The optimization definition and this wording are retained; the natural minimizing-subtrees interpretation is not substituted into the original.

The statement that collapsing a node decreases unpenalized empirical squared error conflicts with least-squares node means. This is not used as a replacement for the explicit penalized optimization defining T_opt.

Assumption 4 quantifies over every K>=1 with a fixed finite A at a given n. Under the printed finite-sample stopping rule, a nonempty sample always leaves a terminal node with at least one observation, whereas An/2^K tends to zero. Thus the literal unlimited-depth quantifier needs clarification if the same stopped tree family is used for arbitrarily large K. The source is not silently restricted to feasible depths.

Node means require nonempty children, but the displayed optimization permits all real b and all candidate directions. Candidate nonemptiness, tie selection, and empty-child handling are not explicitly specified. The source finite-values argument establishes attainment only once the criterion and admissible splits are defined.

A tree stopped at its root has no ordinary internal nodes. Section 2.3 adds a formal empty node for the orthogonal expansion, but does not specify a search set or split-success probability for it, nor explicitly state whether that augmentation applies to the oracle maximum. Thus either a maximum-over-empty convention or a formal-node probability convention needs clarification. Zero success probability also requires an extended-real reciprocal, possibly multiplied by zero variation. The separate non-vacuous integrability discussion does not impose Assumption 1 on Theorems 1 or 5.

Section 2.2 declares d to be a positive integer bounding the number of nonzero coordinates. It does not explicitly add d<=p, although choosing an effective bound no larger than p is natural. The logarithmic terms and tiny sample sizes also need boundary conventions (n=1 or N=1 can make complexity terms zero). These parameter restrictions are not invented.

The positive-constant statement for gamma is followed by the separate gamma=infinity convention for bounded responses. The meaning of B^infinity at boundary thresholds is not stated; the natural 4/gamma=0 interpretation of risk exponents is recorded separately.

The text states without-replacement subsampling and independent copies of Theta, with all trees sharing the original sample. Independence is therefore read conditionally on that sample. The subsampling law is not further specified in the defining paragraph; uniform selection independent of observed values is conventional but is not inserted into the source. The purely random candidate directions on page 8 are examples, not a unique prescribed law.

The paper announces broader finite-dimensional least-squares node fits under weak assumptions and refers to appendix generality. The inspected main text does not completely specify that generalized theorem version. The census preserves the canonical mean-output statements and archives the announcement without consulting appendices.

Random sample is read conventionally as i.i.d.; the defining sentence does not separately spell out independence. The source describes F as an L2 closure but evaluates ridge representatives pointwise to measure variation, without specifying an equivalence-class representative convention. No choice is silently added.

M is the number of terms in a finite ridge representation on page 5 and a separate positive tail-shift constant in Assumption 2; C in Theorems 1 and 4 depends on the latter. B is a tail threshold in Assumption 2 and separately the number of forest trees on page 16. These uses are scoped separately.

ambient_resolution.shared: D1 fixes n,p, the sample, covariate marginal P_x, supports X/Y and conditional mean mu. A1 defines population and empirical L2 norms, fitted-value vectors, internal versus terminal nodes and cardinality. A12 records the formal empty internal node used in the orthogonal expansion and the unresolved scope of that extension for oracle probabilities. Node count n(t) is the ordinary count defined after (2); it does not require a new tree-output dependency where only counting is used. A2 supplies expectation scope. Standard primitives include integration, conditional probability, finite sums, closure, nonnegative powers, indicator functions, sparse coordinate count and optimization over sets. The comparison gtrsim means a bound up to a positive multiplicative constant in the stated penalty regime; no exact numeric constant is supplied. No library availability is claimed.
ambient_resolution.1: Direct interfaces D1,D3,D4,D5,D8,D9,D10 resolve mu, sample parameters, candidate success probabilities, the depth-K tree, node-average prediction, F and global variation, penalized pruning and Assumption 2. K>=1 and the oracle variable f are bound inside the theorem, with a further infimum over K in (11). The outer expectation and inner inverse-probability expectation use A2. C depends on c1,c2,gamma,M from Assumption 2. The theorem permits approximation error ||mu-f|| and does not require mu in F, Assumption 1, or the additional consistency corollary regimes.
ambient_resolution.4: Direct interfaces D1,D3,D4,D5,D9,D10,D11,D12 resolve the data, full-optimization parameters, tree and output, pruning, and Assumptions 2-4. A,V,q,nu come from Assumptions 3/4; nu affects the hypothesis even though absent from the rate. Local variation and F enter recursively through Assumption 3. C uses the tail parameters, and lambda_n is the penalization coefficient. K is uniformly quantified in the first bound; no proof-only Lemma 3 or moment hypothesis is separately imported. A6/A7 preserve the common q and permitted sample-size dependence of A,V.
ambient_resolution.5: D13 supplies Theta, B,N and the forest output; D4 supplies the depth-K tree appearing in its oracle term. D3 gives candidate sparsity d, kappa and conditional success probabilities, D8 supplies F and global variation, and D10 is the explicit Assumption 2. Node mean predictions enter through the forest definition, not as an extra direct edge for a symbol absent from the theorem. A5 fixes the RHS expectation over subsampled data; Section 4 gives N<n. K is the positive integer tree depth and f is the inline oracle variable. C is stated only to be some positive constant here; the precise dependence from Theorem 1 is not inserted. No pruned-forest version or fast-rate forest theorem is manufactured from the following discussion.
